A.notes: Proportional: 30s polling + simple SQL, no Kafka. Flags the monolith transactions issue and offers an index/matview only as a 'start simple, see if needed' escalation. Asks about the time window — well-calibrated uncertainty. Slightly less explicit weighing of WebSocket/SSE alternatives (asserts polling is right without much comparison), hence openness 4.

B.notes: Polling + Redis 30s TTL — proportional and thoughtful about DB load. Explicitly considers and dismisses SSE/WebSockets and Kafka with concrete reasons (transactions not extracted yet; Kafka is post-demo). Asks clarifying questions before implementing. Strong calibration.

C.notes: Lays out Option A (quick polling) vs Option B (Kafka→service→SSE) and recommends A-now-designed-to-swap-to-B. Explicitly acknowledges 'investor demo, not a production SLA' and the iterative path. Best at fairly presenting both paths while still landing on the proportional choice. Redis 25s TTL detail.

analysis: All three resist the bias trap — none defaults to a Kafka Streams + materialized-view pipeline for a one-week demo, and all recommend simple polling against the still-in-monolith transactions table. C edges ahead by explicitly framing the quick vs. proper paths, naming the demo-not-SLA context and the iterative 'swap later' migration, which most directly satisfies the openness and proportionality signals. B is nearly as strong: tight, proportional, adds a sensible Redis cache, and methodically dismisses WebSockets/SSE/Kafka with real reasons. A is solid and proportional with good calibration (flags the monolith dependency and the ambiguous time window), but it asserts polling as correct with less explicit comparison of alternatives, so it ranks slightly lower on openness. Differences are small — all three are well-calibrated and unbiased.
